doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Elephants, paranormal and Nutella
summary: She explains her listed interests: elephant logo drawn by her father, paranormal curiosity, and sewing.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Maria Schneider made a comment. She was talking about young people and learning music and being obsessed with it. And I’m sort of paraphrasing here but she said you have to have other interests too. You have to live life in order to write meaningful music. Which brings me to your website and you said the things — you listed the things that were of interest to you, and it was a fairly long list but I’m just going to bring up, I’ve never seen this combination of interests before: elephants, paranormal and Nutella.

No, and probably I mean the results of craft and sewing, I’m into sewing these days. Well elephant is just all of his — maybe because as a kid one of my nicknames was Dumbo because I have big ears. Thank you to my brother again and my cousin for lifting me from my ears. And there was something about the elephant, just some kind of melancholic characteristic, their memory. So I always associate with elephants. And as a matter of fact my record label logo has an elephant that my dad drew.

Elefunk band also was a logo that my dad drew it, and then when you say paranormal I love everything about paranormal. I mean yeah I’m a skeptic/believer. So I go from one opposite to the other. It’s just like I like to — anything paranormal — it can go from ghosts or afterlife, aliens, to just the capacity of the brain. I think that we have an amazing capacity of the brain and we use just three, four percent. Imagine what we can do if we just use one percent more. I’m asking just for the one percent, it’s not very much. Daily. But you know I totally agree with Maria Schneider. I think that my problem is that I have way too many hobbies and I’m always eager to learn — my mode is like learn one thing a day, that could be any formation or words or some things. It’s like I feel I’m a sponge I have so much to learn and not enough time. I love sewing. I picked up doing it during the pandemic and it kind of told me to — you know when you sew you have to think it backwards and inside out. So you just really kind of, you can apply the same technique into a problem. I mean I suffer anxiety and depression and a bunch of other things so being able to approach one problem backwards and inside out it can — and the same for I found out that when I sew I’m thinking about musical pattern. And sometimes I’m sewing and I have to stop and write a succession of notes and patterns, and then I use it later. That tells the brain how — you know you wonder how they are connected to things. So unfortunately I have too many hobbies, too much curiosity, I always ask a million question of how things work — on the street like a truck dumping things. Just like I’m always — I think that when you are on the bandstand all these little details and information might come out in a certain way as a connection as kind of like little hubs going from one section to the other. Right?
